concepts.label: managed-object
concepts.gloss: A managed compute-domain object, such as a physical server or hosted container, whose operational state is monitored and against which events and alarms are raised.
concepts.example: node-14 is a monitored server, while ctr-app-node14 is a monitored application container hosted on that server.

concepts.label: event
concepts.gloss: A discrete syslog message or SNMP trap reporting an occurrence on a managed object, which may serve as an input to fault detection without itself necessarily representing an active alarm condition.
concepts.example: trap-cpu-node14-t0 is an SNMP trap emitted for node-14 when a CPU-related occurrence is detected.

concepts.label: alarm
concepts.gloss: A fault-management record representing an active or reportable abnormal condition on a managed object and carrying both a perceived severity and an X.733-style probable-cause code.
concepts.example: alarm-node14-overtemp represents an overheating condition on node-14, with severity critical and probable cause thermalTrip.

concepts.label: severity
concepts.gloss: The perceived operational impact or urgency assigned to an alarm, expressed as an ordered alarm level such as critical, major, minor, or warning.
concepts.example: The severity of alarm-node14-overtemp is critical, indicating the highest listed level of operational urgency.

concepts.label: probable-cause
concepts.gloss: An X.733-style categorical cause code attached to an alarm that identifies the fault type believed most likely to explain the reported condition.
concepts.example: alarm-node14-overtemp carries thermalTrip as its probable cause; a cooling-hardware alarm could instead carry fanFailure.

concepts.label: clear
concepts.gloss: A fault-management notification or state-transition record that terminates a specified previously raised alarm because its abnormal condition is no longer active.
concepts.example: clear-alarm-node14-overtemp clears alarm-node14-overtemp after node-14 returns to an acceptable temperature.
